transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump is marking Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery.
The president and first lady participated in a wreath laying at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
Trump is also speaking at the cemetery's memorial amphitheater at the Sauer.
Communities across the nation are holding observances of their own.
House Republicans have chosen a new leader as they prepared to enter the minority in January.
NPR's Barbara Sprout reports Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan will take the helm when Democrats regain control.
Jordan was selected as Republican's top leader in the House after a vote-by-secret ballot.
After the crushing defeat for Republicans in the midterms, House Speaker Mike Johnson said he would step down as the top House Republican.
In Jordan, Republicans have chosen someone with significant experience on the Judiciary and Oversight Committees.
Both panels are critical to Democrats' plans come January.
Jordan told colleagues his leadership experience on those committees would help him navigate Democratic investigations.
His selection also shows the Republicans are looking for a clean break from the last leadership slate.
That's NPR's Barbara Sprout reporting from the Capitol.
Hundreds of schools in Italy, Scotland, Ireland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports on what appears to be the latest coordinated effort to sow chaos and disruption across Europe.
Police in Northern Ireland said the more than 300 affected schools received the same chilling email.
A copy of the message sent to Italian schools seen by NPR said, quote, "I have prepared for this for a long time, to kill every one of you."
It said an explosive with a remote detonator had been placed in the building.
The message caused panic in schools with many evacuating.
Police in Scotland and Northern Ireland described the message as a hoax.
Italy's defense minister, Guido Rossetto, said it was part of an effort to create panic and disruption in European countries.
For NPR News, I'm Ruth Sherlock in London.
The relationship between the world's two biggest economies is evolving.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the U.S. Treasury Secretary is calling for more balance between his country and China.
Treasury Secretary Scott Besant says the U.S. needs to produce more and China needs to consume more.
Besant spoke at a New York gala last night ahead of President Trump's visit to Shenzhen next week, where he'll meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
China's consumption is likely to get a boost from Singles Day, which starts today.
The online shopping promotion is a kind of cross between Prime Day, Black Friday and Valentine's Day.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
On Wall Street, the Dow was up 68 points.
This is NPR News.
Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain undecided as election officials continue counting ballots.
In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola expanded her lead over Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Tuesday's update.
Rank choice tabulation could determine the winner with that count scheduled for November 18th.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Cologne maintains a narrow lead over Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Counties are reviewing outstanding ballots and have until Friday to certify their results.
President Trump has nominated Matt Zandi for a seat on the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.
NPR's Andrea Shue reports the trial lawyer has been serving as chief of staff for the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.
If confirmed, Zandi would be the third Republican at the EEOC, further cementing the party's control over the agency in charge of enforcing civil rights protections for workers.
Zandi would fill the seat of former Commissioner Jocelyn Samuels, a Democrat fired by Trump last year.
Under Trump, the EEOC has pushed back against DEI, changing regulations and filing lawsuits challenging programs that aim to level the playing field for workers historically marginalized by race or gender.
The agency also dropped cases it was pursuing on behalf of transgender and non-binary individuals, and stepped up litigation related to religious liberties.
Zandi's nomination now goes to the Senate. Andrea Shue, NPR News.
On Wall Street, the Dow up 68 points, the NASDAQ up 474. This is NPR News in Washington.
